dct_description_sm: The purpose of the project is to fill region-specific data gaps related to human chemical exposures among First Nations of the Northwest Territories and Yukon. This research is relying on stored samples from previous human biomonitoring projects completed in Ts'ueh Nda (NT), Katlodeeche (NT), Tthets'hk'edl (NT), Deh Gh Got' (NT), Sambaa Ke (NT), Ka'a'gee Tu (NT), K'asho Got'ine (NT), Dln (NT), Tult'a (NT), and Old Crow (YT). This research involves the measurement of chlorinated paraffins, per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a chlorpyrifos metabolite (TCPy), chlorinated paraffins (SCCP and MCCP), as well as dioxins and dioxin-like compounds (DLCs) in stored urine and plasma samples. Each individual with plasma and urine within the biobank will receive a personalized letter describing the levels of analytes measured in their samples.
